events.title: Battle of Stirling Bridge
events.description: Scottish forces led by William Wallace and Andrew Moray defeated a larger English army under John de Warenne, Earl of Surrey, and Hugh de Cressingham at the River Forth near Stirling.
events.significance: The victory was a major early triumph in the First War of Scottish Independence and established Wallace as a national hero, showing that the English army could be defeated.

events.title: Construction Begins on the Pentagon
events.description: Ground was broken for the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia, to consolidate the War Department's scattered offices into one headquarters as the United States prepared for possible entry into World War II.
events.significance: The Pentagon became the headquarters of the U.S. Department of Defense and one of the world's largest office buildings, symbolizing American military power.

events.title: Chilean Coup d'État
events.description: The Chilean military, led by General Augusto Pinochet, overthrew the democratically elected government of President Salvador Allende, who died in the presidential palace during the attack.
events.significance: The coup began a 17-year military dictatorship marked by human rights abuses and radical free-market reforms, and it remains a defining event of Cold War Latin America.

events.title: September 11 Attacks
events.description: Nineteen al-Qaeda hijackers seized four commercial airliners, crashing two into the World Trade Center in New York City and one into the Pentagon, while a fourth crashed in a field in Pennsylvania after passengers resisted. Nearly 3,000 people were killed.
events.significance: The deadliest terrorist attack in history prompted the U.S. War on Terror, the invasions of Afghanistan and later Iraq, the creation of the Department of Homeland Security, and sweeping changes in global security policy.

events.title: Birth of Mathematician Robert Langlands Honored? Not Applicable: Beatles Record Debut Single
events.description: On this date, the Beatles recorded their debut single sessions at EMI's Abbey Road Studios, with Ringo Starr drumming on 'Love Me Do' for the first time in a full session with the group.
events.significance: The session was a key step in the band's rise to global fame and marked the start of a transformation in popular music.
